description: The Greenstreets dataset lists the sites of the NYC Greenstreets program, which began in 1996 as a partnership between NYC Parks and the city transportation department to turn unused road areas into green spaces that beautify neighbourhoods, improve air quality, reduce air temperature and calm traffic. Greenstreets later became part of the city's green infrastructure, and some sites contain bioswales or rain gardens that divert or filter stormwater. The data use the standard New York projection in feet and square feet, and a data dictionary is linked. The catalogue entry offers six resources, JSON, XML, CSV, KML in two forms and GeoJSON, and shows the dataset last updated on 3 September 2026. Coverage: one city, site-level. Access: free downloads; the licence is not stated on the page read. Caveats: only some sites function as stormwater infrastructure and the dataset does not flag which, and no performance data are included. It supports street-scale green infrastructure and stormwater capacity analysis, and relates to the NYC Green Infrastructure Program case study and the Seattle layer in the catalogue.
